channel.title: Sankaku Complex — AniNews Hub RSS
channel.description: Latest stories from Sankaku Complex through AniNews Hub.

item.title: Night Shift Nurses Returns With New Free-to-Play Card Battle RPG
item.description: Japanese eroge series Night Shift Nurses (Yakin Byoutou) is returning with a new free-to-play card-battling RPG, bringing back heroines from across the franchise’s history.

item.title: Madoka Magica Smartwatches Transform Characters When Your Heart Rate Rises
item.description: A new collection of Puella Magi Madoka Magica smartwatches is launching in Japan, featuring interactive watch faces that transform characters into magical girls when the wearer’s heart rate increases.

item.title: Niconico Is Shutting Down on Nintendo Switch, Confirms No Plans for Switch 2 Support
item.description: Japanese video-sharing platform Niconico is officially ending support for the Nintendo Switch after nearly a decade, with operator Dwango confirming that it has no plans to bring the service to Nintendo Switch 2.

item.title: Palworld Developer Rejects Live-Service Model With Tons of DLC & Microtransactions
item.description: Palworld developer Pocketpair has explained why it has no interest in turning its popular monster-collecting survival game into a massive live-service platform filled with downloadable content and microtransactions.

item.title: Avatar Creators Defend Korra Against Critics, Blame “Misogyny” & “Homophobia”
item.description: Avatar: The Last Airbender creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko have defended Korra against criticism from fans, arguing that misogyny and homophobia have contributed to the character’s controversial reputation.

item.title: Mosque’s Religious Booth at Japanese Elementary School Festival Sparks Criticism
item.description: A mosque’s participation in a community festival held at a public elementary school in Osaka Prefecture has drawn criticism on Japanese social media, with some users questioning whether religious outreach should be permitted on school grounds.

item.title: Silent Hill & Fatal Frame Creators: “Women Dominate Japanese Horror Because Oppression”
item.description: Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto and Fatal Frame creator Makoto Shibata have discussed why women frequently appear as both protagonists and terrifying ghosts in Japanese horror, suggesting that the genre’s traditions are closely connected to the “historical oppression of women”.

item.title: Pokemon Company Cracks Down on Scalpers as Websites Ban Bulk Pokemon Card Listings
item.description: The Pokémon Company is introducing new restrictions on Pokémon Trading Card Game resales in Japan, partnering with major online marketplaces to combat scalping and potentially fraudulent listings.

item.title: Hong Kong Billionaire Proposes Selling Defective Condoms to Increase Birth Rates
item.description: A prominent Hong Kong businessman has sparked widespread outrage after suggesting that governments should force manufacturers to sell deliberately defective condoms to increase birth rates by causing unintended pregnancies.

item.title: Malfoid Still the Cutest Tsundere in New AI-Generated Anime Parodies
item.description: Internet users obsessed with the Malfoid meme, which involves a genderswapped version of Harry Potter character Draco Malfoy, have produced yet more AI-generated anime parodies where Malfoid acts cute and tsundere – with these latest videos naturally employing yet more anime tropes.

item.title: Man Faces Police Investigation After Doing Pull-Ups on 1,500-Year-Old Chinese Temple
item.description: A man in China is facing a formal police investigation after filming himself performing pull-ups on a wooden beam at the 1,500-year-old Hanging Temple in Shanxi Province, sparking outrage over the potential damage to the historic structure.

item.title: Dragon Quest Creator Yuji Horii Makes Entire Mystery Game Using AI in 30 Minutes
item.description: Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii has released a free mystery adventure game that he says took just 30 minutes to create using artificial intelligence, demonstrating how dramatically game development has changed since he began his career more than four decades ago.

item.title: Epic Games Announces Major AI Push as Developers Reportedly Told to Stop Coding by Hand
item.description: Epic Games is undergoing a major restructuring to prioritize artificial intelligence, with CEO Tim Sweeney confirming that the company is moving developers around to accelerate AI adoption across its projects.

item.title: California Orders Company to Stop Hosting Human vs. Robot Cage Fights
item.description: California regulators have ordered a San Francisco robotics company to stop organizing unauthorized human-versus-robot cage fights after a viral event featured a social media influencer battling three humanoid machines.

item.title: Physical Fitness Declining Among Japanese Women in Their 30s and 40s
item.description: Physical fitness among Japanese women in their 30s and 40s has been declining over the past 25 years, with experts suggesting that the unequal burden of housework and childcare is preventing many women from exercising regularly.

item.title: Live-Action Naruto Movie Director Promises More News Soon
item.description: The upcoming live-action Naruto movie has received an update from director Destin Daniel Cretton, who confirmed that work is continuing on the long-awaited Hollywood adaptation and teased more announcements in the near future.

item.title: Two Men Killed, Eight Injured in Separate Japanese Festival Float Accidents
item.description: Two men were killed and eight others injured in separate accidents involving traditional Japanese festival floats in Osaka Prefecture on October 10, including one incident in which a massive wooden float overturned during a high-speed turn.

item.title: Student Suspended After Bringing “Death Note” to School, Continuing 20-Year Trend
item.description: A middle school student in Massachusetts has been suspended after bringing a notebook inspired by the popular anime and manga series Death Note to school, prompting a police investigation. However, this is far from the first time the fictional notebook has caused controversy in American schools.

item.title: Nintendo Latin America Confirms It Has No Plans to Abandon Physical Games
item.description: Nintendo has confirmed that it currently has no plans to stop selling physical games, reassuring fans concerned about the gaming industry’s increasing shift toward digital-only releases.

item.title: Konami Already Planning Second & Third Waves of Silent Hill Games
item.description: Konami is already considering a second and third wave of Silent Hill games following the revival of its long-running survival horror franchise, according to series producer Motoi Okamoto.

item.title: Masashi Kishimoto Announces Naruto: Shadow Rising
item.description: Naruto creator Masashi Kishimoto is returning with a new manga titled Naruto: Shadow Rising, while the franchise is also getting a four-episode crossover anime with the classic ninja series Ninku.

item.title: Japanese Twin Brothers Arrested for Stealing Copper Roof from Shrine
item.description: Two 37-year-old twin brothers have been arrested in Japan on suspicion of stealing copper roofing from a mountain shrine, as police investigate a series of similar thefts targeting religious sites across Kochi Prefecture.

item.title: Nexus Mods Accused of Removing Popular Elden Ring Mod Without Warning
item.description: Nexus Mods is facing criticism yet again after allegedly removing several files associated with a free Elden Ring mod without warning, prompting its creator to move his work to another modding platform.

item.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Full of Dark-Skinned Characters, Gays, and Fully Trained Avatars
item.description: The newest entry in the beloved Avatar series, Avatar: Seven Havens, has somehow turned out to be even more despised and criticized than Legend of Korra, with the show having a surplus of dark-skinned characters, homosexuals, and an avatar who doesn’t seem to need any training.
